title: Idempotency key rotation, retry classifier, and per-SDK ergonomic helpers
creator: Avery Chen
description: Goal: Provide a cross-SDK (Python/TypeScript/Go) specification and ergonomic helpers for idempotency key generation/rotation, a canonical retryable-error taxonomy, and sensible default backoff profiles. This ticket bundles: (1) a clear id-key contract (format, TTL, rotation semantics, server acceptance), (2) a retry-classifier mapping common transport/HTTP/gRPC errors to retryable/non-retryable categories with rationale, and (3) small per-language helper libraries that expose defaults + easy overrides for power users. Motivation: Teams keep reimplementing brittle idempotency and retry logic leading to duplicate work, subtle data-corruption windows in streaming flows, and inconsistent customer experiences across SDKs. Deliverables should be implementation-agnostic guidance plus thin SDK helpers that reduce footguns while remaining easy to opt out of.
acceptance_criteria: Specification doc published describing id-key format, rotation TTL, header name(s), and server-side handling semantics
Canonical retry taxonomy mapping (HTTP status families, gRPC codes, network errors, server throttling) with per-class retry decision and example code
Default backoff parameters for each SDK (initial_delay, max_delay, multiplier, jitter strategy) documented and implemented in SDK helper APIs
Example snippets in Python/TS/Go demonstrating id-key creation, rotation, and safe retries for both unary and streaming requests
End-to-end integration test that exercises duplicate suppression window for streaming append operations and verifies no double-apply under retry storms
Rollout plan with feature flag and metrics (duplicate_count, retried_requests, successful_retries) defined and wired to console dashboard
implementation_notes:
API surface: expose a small helper object in each SDK: IdempotencyManager + RetryPolicy. IdempotencyManager responsibilities: generate_key(operation_name, version_hint), rotate_key(key) (returns new key and the old key expiry), and key_metadata(key) to allow apps to expose user-facing debug ids. Default id-key format: v1::<unix_ms>-<rand8hex>-<svc-short>-<op-hash>. TTL/rotation: keys are valid for 24 hours by default; rotation window is configurable. Header convention: X-Redwood-Idempotency (HTTP) and metadata pair 'redwood-idempotency' (gRPC). Backoff defaults (opinionated): initial=100ms, multiplier=2.0, max=10s, jitter=full (random between 0 and current_delay). For streaming idempotency/deduping: suggest a 30s dedup window for chunked append operations by default, configurable per route. Retry taxonomy (summary): retryable_transient = {DNS timeout, TCP reset, ECONNREFUSED (on transient), HTTP 502/503/504, gRPC UNAVAILABLE/DEADLINE_EXCEEDED, 429 (rate limit -> backoff + optional throttle header) } ; non_retryable = {HTTP 400/401/403/404, gRPC INVALID_ARGUMENT/PERMISSION_DENIED}. Throttles: 429 should be treated as retryable but with increased base backoff and honoring Retry-After header if present. Edge cases: idempotent-safe operations vs side-effectful operations: default policy is optimistic: most write-like operations require an explicit idempotency key; SDK helper will raise if trying to call write endpoint without key unless user passes allow_unsafe_writes=true. Example snippets:

Python:
from redwood_sdk import IdempotencyManager, RetryPolicy
idm = IdempotencyManager(service_name="ingest")
key = idm.generate_key("append_event", version_hint="v1")
policy = RetryPolicy.from_defaults()
resp = client.append(event, idempotency_key=key, retry_policy=policy)

TypeScript:
import { IdempotencyManager, RetryPolicy } from '@redwood/sdk'
const idm = new IdempotencyManager('ingest')
const key = idm.generateKey('append_event', { versionHint: 'v1' })
const policy = RetryPolicy.defaults()
await client.append(event, { idempotencyKey: key, retryPolicy: policy })

Go:
idm := sdk.NewIdempotencyManager("ingest")
key := idm.GenerateKey("append_event", "v1")
policy := sdk.DefaultRetryPolicy()
resp, err := client.Append(ctx, event, sdk.WithIdempotencyKey(key), sdk.WithRetryPolicy(policy))

Implementation detail: helpers should be small and pure; do NOT implement server-side dedupe here. SDKs will surface metrics and expose hooks so servers can record key acceptance vs duplicate detection.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge spec doc and SDK interface PRs behind an SDK feature flag (enable_idempotency_helper). 2) Publish SDK minor releases with feature opt-in. 3) Enable in a small set of internal services (ingest, jobs) using canary cohort (5% of traffic). 4) Monitor duplicate_count and retried_requests; iterate on defaults if duplicates increase. 5) After 2 weeks of stable metrics, flip feature flag to 50%, then GA. Provide a migration guide for customers who previously relied on custom id-key formats.
testing_plan: - Unit tests for generator determinism, rotation TTL enforcement, and key parsing. - Integration tests that simulate transient network failures (tcp reset, connection timeout) and verify SDK retries respect policy and do not cause double-apply when id-key is present. - Streaming tests: simulate duplicate fragment delivery and verify server-side dedupe window prevents double-apply; ensure SDK respects dedup window by rotating keys when appropriate. - Chaos test: high-retry flood with 429s to ensure backoff parameters and Retry-After handling avoid cascading failures. - Cross-language conformance test harness (fixtures) to ensure parity across Python/TS/Go implementations.
comments: 2025-02-16 Avery Chen: Initial draft uploaded. Focused on pragmatic defaults to reduce cognitive load for app teams. Left placeholder for exact jitter strategy — leaning full jitter per AWS Exponential Backoff Best Practices.

2025-02-17 Priya Khatri: Review — please add guidance for customer-supplied keys vs SDK-generated keys. PM suggests defaults should prefer SDK generation for new apps but allow override for legacy integration.

2025-02-18 Marta Silva: Eng review — discussed the security implications of id-key format. Agreed to avoid embedding PII; use op-hash instead of full resource identifiers. Also requested a shorter default dedup window (30s) for high-volume streams.

2025-02-19 Luis Ortega: Implementation note — will implement Python helper first and reuse core TS/Go algorithms from a small reference library. We will expose environment variable to change default TTL during canary.
2025-02-20 Avery Chen: Updated spec to include header names and Retry-After handling for 429s. Marking planned -> ready for implementation once design doc sign-off.
